review: i don't have an account and i'm not making one, so i don't know why i'm typing this. "kitchen light at six" is four minutes of nothing happening and it's the only piece of music in about nine years that hasn't tried to get something out of me. no build. no key change at the exact point where you're supposed to feel it. it just sits there with you. i've played it maybe two hundred times, always at 2am, always with the kettle on. i left a church because everything in it was engineered to produce a response in me and i could feel the engineering. this isn't engineered. or if it is, whoever did it is better than the people i left, which i suppose is also possible. anyway. five stars. that's the first thing i've rated in my life.
